keyTakeaways: Use तुम for a wife, not आप: in a 19,177,172-token Hindi news corpus आप appears 12,335 times against 750 for तुम, and that आप-heavy register is a stranger's rather than a spouse's.
Aim for about 96 characters — the median personal message across 197 messages on SubhSandesh's 198 partner-birthday pages, with 106 of the 197 under 100 characters.

faqs.question: Should I use तुम or आप for my wife's birthday wish in Hindi?
faqs.answer: तुम, in almost every household. आप between spouses reads as either formality or a deliberate old-fashioned respect, and it is the register print Hindi defaults to — 12,335 आप against 750 तुम in a 19-million-token news corpus — which is exactly why copied wishes sound distant.

faqs.question: Is तू rude if I use it for my wife?
faqs.answer: Only if तू is not already how you speak to each other. तू is intimate between people who use it and insulting between people who do not; there is no neutral reading. If you have to ask, use तुम.

faqs.question: How long should a Hindi birthday wish for a wife be?
faqs.answer: About 96 characters. That is the median personal message across 197 messages on SubhSandesh's 198 partner-birthday pages, and 106 of the 197 are under 100 characters — roughly two lines of Devanagari.

faqs.question: Do I write it in Devanagari or in English letters?
faqs.answer: Whichever she reads faster. If she was schooled entirely in English she may speak Hindi fluently and read Devanagari slowly, in which case a Roman transliteration is the kinder choice. Sending both costs nothing.

faqs.question: Should I post the wish in the family WhatsApp group or send it privately?
faqs.answer: Both, in two different versions. Keep pet names and anything physical out of the group version, and send the pet-name line one-to-one — public and private display of affection are separate measurable behaviours, not two doses of the same thing.

faqs.question: What is the difference between बधाई and शुभकामनाएं?
faqs.answer: बधाई is the everyday congratulation and शुभकामनाएं the ceremonial one. In the same Hindi corpus बधाई appears 739 times against 214 for शुभकामनाएं, so बधाई is the warmer choice for a wife and शुभकामनाएं the safer one addressed upward.

faqs.question: My wife replies in आप. Am I being too casual with तुम?
faqs.answer: No. Spousal address in India has never been symmetrical — fieldwork records a widely prevalent custom in which a wife uses the plural respect form to her husband and avoids his name entirely. Matching her आप out of politeness is what reads as distance.

faqs.question: What pronoun do I use for birthday wishes for a boss in Hindi?
faqs.answer: आप, with no exceptions. आपको जन्मदिन की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं is the safe formula, and सर or साहब works as the address term — both are live in written Hindi at 517 and 895 uses respectively.

faqs.question: Can I use the same Hindi wish for my wife and my boss?
faqs.answer: Not without rewriting the verb. Changing तुम to आप changes the agreement on every verb and possessive in the sentence, so a wife's line cannot be reused for a boss by swapping one word.

faqs.question: Is it wrong to use my wife's name in the birthday wish?
faqs.answer: No, and it usually helps. Name avoidance in Indian marriages traditionally ran the other way — the wife avoiding the husband's name — and studies of Indian address terms record both spouses using names as a recent change rather than a breach.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Birthday Wishes for Wife in Hindi: तुम, Not आप, and Why

Write it in तुम. Hindi gives you three words for "you" — आप, तुम and तू — and for a wife तुम fits almost every household, तू only if you already speak that way. Keep it short: across 197 personal messages on SubhSandesh's 198 partner-birthday pages, the median message is **96 characters**, and 106 of the 197 sit under 100 — two lines of Devanagari.

Then decide where it goes before you write it, because a wish sent privately and the same wish posted to the family WhatsApp group are not the same message — and only 37.9% of birthday-page creators password-protect the page, against 43.9% site-wide. Below: the pronoun measured against 19 million words of Hindi, five wishes with character counts, the public-private split, and the आप version for a boss.

## What a Hindi birthday wish decides before it says anything

Hindi has a three-way second person: आप is honorific and takes plural agreement, तुम is familiar, तू is intimate or insulting depending on who is speaking. English has one "you", so an English wish can be warm or cool in its adjectives; a Hindi wish has declared the relationship by the time it reaches the verb.

Copy a line off a wishes page and you inherit its writer's pronoun, and with it a claim about how close you are. The 198 pages measured here sit on the partner-birthday template — 6.5% of the 3,024 pages built on SubhSandesh since March 2026 — so this is the spousal register.

## The pronoun, measured against 19 million words of Hindi

So we counted. The [Leipzig Corpora Collection's Hindi news corpus](https://corpora.uni-leipzig.de/en?corpusId=hin_news_2011_1M) holds 19,177,172 tokens and returns absolute frequencies. Queried 27 August 2026:

- आप — 12,335 · तुम — 750 · तू — 236
- आपको — 6,884 · तुम्हें — 201 · तुझे — 43
- आपका — 1,759 · तुम्हारा — 118 · तेरा — 189

Of the 13,321 nominative tokens आप takes **92.6%**, तुम 5.6%, तू 1.8%. आप outnumbers तुम 16.4 to one.

That is not an instruction to use आप. It is a warning: print Hindi is overwhelmingly आप because journalism quotes strangers and addresses readers, never a spouse — which is why copied wishes read like bank letters.

One cell is odd. तेरा (189) outranks तुम्हारा (118), though तू is a third of तुम in the nominative — तू's possessive survives in quoted lyrics and verse where its subject form does not, which is why तेरा reads as poetry rather than rudeness.

## Five birthday wishes for your wife in Hindi, with character counts

Each is under the measured 96-character median; counts are of the Devanagari string.

### 1. The default private wish — 63 characters

जन्मदिन मुबारक, मेरी जान। तुम्हारे साथ हर साल पहले से बेहतर है।

*Janmadin mubārak, merī jān. Tumhāre sāth har sāl pahle se behtar hai.* — "Happy birthday, my life. Every year with you is better than the last." तुम, via तुम्हारे; the pet name मेरी जान is what makes it unpostable in a group.

### 2. The shortest one that still says something — 37 characters

जन्मदिन की बधाई। घर तुमसे घर लगता है।

*Janmadin kī badhāī. Ghar tumse ghar lagtā hai.* — "Happy birthday. Home feels like home because of you." बधाई is the everyday congratulation word — 739 uses in the corpus above, against 214 for शुभकामनाएं — and at 37 characters this survives as a photo caption.

### 3. For a specific thing rather than a general one — 61 characters

तुम्हें जन्मदिन मुबारक। तुम्हारी हँसी मेरी सबसे अच्छी आदत है।

*Tumhen janmadin mubārak. Tumhārī haṁsī merī sabse acchī ādat hai.* — "Happy birthday to you. Your laugh is my favourite habit." Swap हँसी for whatever is true; a named detail is the one thing a 330-item list cannot supply.

### 4. The version you can post publicly — 61 characters

जन्मदिन की बहुत बहुत बधाई। तुम हमारे घर की सबसे बड़ी ताकत हो।

*Janmadin kī bahut bahut badhāī. Tum hamāre ghar kī sabse baṛī tākat ho.* — "Very many happy returns. You are the greatest strength of our home." Still तुम, no pet name, so it survives a group with her parents in it.

### 5. For couples who already speak in तू — 48 characters

तेरे बिना कुछ भी अपना नहीं लगता। जन्मदिन मुबारक।

*Tere binā kuchh bhī apnā nahīṁ lagtā. Janmadin mubārak.* — "Nothing feels like mine without you. Happy birthday." Only if तू is already how you talk; used cold it reads as a stranger being familiar.

## Where it goes changes what it says

A private wish and a posted wish are separate behaviours, not two doses of one thing. The [Public and Private Romantic Display of Affection Scale](https://journals.pan.pl/Content/124290/PDF/2022-03-PPB-rew.pdf) — validated on 894 Polish adults, then on 204 couples (*Polish Psychological Bulletin*, September 2022) — was built with public and private display as separate subscales, because people differ across the two.

Its inconvenient finding: a negative association between age, relationship duration and willingness to show affection, in private *and* in public. Long marriages display less on both dimensions, and tend not to notice.

The public half is not empty ritual either. Among 170 respondents, those who had posted their relationship status reported higher relational satisfaction (M = 5.40) than those who had not (M = 4.53), Cohen's *d* = 1.06 — [Piercy's warranting-theory study](https://kuscholarworks.ku.edu/handle/1808/27653), *Computers in Human Behavior*, November 2015. That sample was US undergraduates, so read it as directional.

So send the pet-name line privately, post the no-pet-name line, and do both. Our data says the private channel is the under-protected one: 37.9% of birthday pages get a password against 43.9% across all page types. If a surprise is meant to be one, gate it — a [birthday page for a partner](https://subhsandesh.in/birthday-gf) takes a password in one field, and the median page is done in 0.9 hours.

## She probably will not answer in the same register

Spousal address in India has never been symmetrical, and there is fieldwork on it. A study of address modes in Mysore district records that "as per a widely prevalent Hindu custom, wife never addresses the husband by his name" and that she "always addresses the husband using the plural form to show respect", while husbands used singular familiar forms back — [Manjulakshi, *Language in India*, 2004](https://www.languageinindia.com/sep2004/manjulakshitermsofaddress2.html).

That study is of Kannada in one district, not Hindi, and treats name-use by both spouses as recent. Take it as evidence the asymmetry is real and old, not as a measurement of your house.

So if she answers in आप, that is not coldness and not a correction of your तुम — it is the older pattern still running, and matching it out of politeness is the move that reads as distance.

## The same sentence for a boss: आप, and nothing else

The far end of the same scale is a manager: same decision, opposite answer. Here आप is the only safe form, and the 92.6% above is finally on your side. Three that work, all inside the 96-character median:

- आपको जन्मदिन की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं। आपके साथ काम करना सीखने जैसा है। — 68 characters. *Āpko janmadin kī hārdik śubhkāmnāen. Āpke sāth kām karnā sīkhne jaisā hai.* "Warm birthday wishes. Working with you is like being taught."
- जन्मदिन मुबारक हो, सर। आपका मार्गदर्शन हमेशा काम आया है। — 56 characters. *Janmadin mubārak ho, sar. Āpkā mārgdarśan hameśā kām āyā hai.* "Happy birthday, sir. Your guidance has always been useful."
- आपको जन्मदिन की बधाई। आने वाला साल आपके लिए शानदार हो। — 54 characters. *Āpko janmadin kī badhāī. Āne vālā sāl āpke liye śāndār ho.* "Happy birthday. May the coming year be splendid for you."

Two word choices matter. शुभकामनाएं is ceremonial, बधाई everyday — 214 against 739 in the corpus — so शुभकामनाएं is safer upward, बधाई warmer for a manager you know.

सर appears 517 times against 895 for साहब, so both are live; सर fits an office. Send it one-to-one, never in the team group, where a wish reads as a performance.

## Register by relationship, side by side

The three contexts differ in pronoun, word choice and destination.

| Writing to | Pronoun | Congratulation word | Length to aim for | Where it goes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wife, privately | तुम (तू only if you already speak it) | जन्मदिन मुबारक | 96 characters — median of 197 real messages | One-to-one chat, or a password-protected page (37.9% do) |
| Wife, in a family group | तुम, no pet name | जन्मदिन की बधाई | Under 96 characters, no physical detail | Group post, private version sent separately |
| Boss | आप only | जन्मदिन की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं | 96 characters, no nickname | One-to-one chat or email, never the team channel |

The length target is identical in all three rows. Only the pronoun and the destination change, because length is not where formality lives in Hindi.

## When a Hindi wish is the wrong choice

If your wife speaks Hindi but does not read Devanagari fluently — common for anyone schooled entirely in English — a Devanagari line makes her work to read an affectionate sentence. Send the transliteration instead, or both. And if she is in the same room, close the laptop.

Interactive extras are oversold. Of the 195 birthday pages that added a quiz, only 28 were ever played — 14.4%. Senders build games; recipients read the message and stop.

Birthday views also skew less mobile than the site average, 48.6% against 51.0%, so a page built for a phone may be opened on a laptop. [Browse the templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) and pick for the message, not the quiz — or for an anniversary, an [anniversary page for a partner](https://subhsandesh.in/anniversary-gf).

Two honest limits. Our data has no language field and no relationship field, so the 96-character median is a partner-birthday figure, not a wife-in-Hindi figure, and no Hindi-specific number is claimed above. And every Devanagari line here was composed for this article and not checked by a native Hindi reader: the corpus frequencies are verifiable, the idiom and gender agreement are not.

## Sources

- [Leipzig Corpora Collection, Hindi news corpus `hin_news_2011_1M`](https://corpora.uni-leipzig.de/en?corpusId=hin_news_2011_1M) — frequencies retrieved 27 August 2026.
- Kocur, Prusik and Konopka, [Public and Private Romantic Display of Affection Scale](https://journals.pan.pl/Content/124290/PDF/2022-03-PPB-rew.pdf), *Polish Psychological Bulletin*, 26 September 2022.
- Piercy, [Making it Facebook official](https://kuscholarworks.ku.edu/handle/1808/27653), *Computers in Human Behavior*, 26 November 2015.
- Manjulakshi, [Modes of Address in Kannada](https://www.languageinindia.com/sep2004/manjulakshitermsofaddress2.html), *Language in India*, September 2004.

failed.item: The post contains at least one claim none of the top 5 pages make
failed.why: STRUCTURAL — this is where the mandatory language blocker lands, and it lands here because in a language post the differentiating claim IS the script content. The claim none of the four ranking results makes is that a Hindi birthday wish for a wife belongs in तुम rather than आप, evidenced by the five composed wish lines, their Roman transliterations and the honorific guidance for wife versus boss. Every one of those Devanagari strings was machine-composed for this article and is unverified, so the differentiating claim is not yet established. No citation can close this: the corpus frequencies (आप 12,335, तुम 750, तू 236) are independently checkable and are not what is in doubt — the idiom, gender agreement and honorific register of the composed lines are, and only a fluent Hindi reader can adjudicate them. Closes when a native Hindi reader reviews the five wife wishes, the three boss wishes, the table's Devanagari cells and the Devanagari inside the FAQs and signs off. Do not publish before that.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Four results rank for this query and two of them are not articles — a Pinterest board and a bare exact-match domain — so the bar is low, but the reason to cite this page is specific rather than comparative: it is the only page on the query that measures the pronoun decision instead of assuming it (आप 12,335, तुम 750, तू 236 in the 19,177,172-token Leipzig Hindi news corpus, retrieved 2026-08-27), and the only one that treats a wish posted to a family WhatsApp group as a different message from the same wish sent privately, with a first-party 37.9%-versus-43.9% password-protect gap behind that claim. Two real weaknesses. There is no open-access, peer-reviewed study of Hindi spousal address that this agent could reach — the closest match (Rahimi & Bassiri on Iranian spousal address forms) was unreachable on every attempt and the best Hindi politeness paper is paywalled — so the Indian-context evidence is a 2004 Kannada study, labelled as such in the body. And the differentiating content is Devanagari that no agent can verify, which is why the originality item is failed rather than passed; a native reader's sign-off is a precondition of publishing, not a nice-to-have. Domain authority against a 330-item content farm and a national news portal is unaddressed by anything in this post, and ranking depends on backlinks and time rather than on this page's contents.
